subject: ss-medical-oncology
title: Mesothelioma and thymic tumours: diagnosis, staging and multimodal therapy

steps.tx: Malignant **pleural mesothelioma** is an aggressive neoplasm arising from mesothelial surfaces, strongly linked to prior occupational or environmental **asbestos exposure**. The disease typically manifests after a prolonged latency period of 30 to 50 years following asbestos inhalation. Most affected patients present with insidious chest wall pain, shortness of breath, and recurrent unilateral pleural effusions, highlighting the critical importance of a thorough occupational history during initial clinical evaluation.

steps.tx: Scan shows circumferential nodular thickening of the right **pleural rind** with mediastinal and fissural involvement plus unilateral **pleural effusion**. The pattern reflects malignant growth along mesothelial surfaces after **asbestos exposure**. It explains chest pain and breathlessness and supports careful occupational history taking when this classic rind and fluid combination is seen.
steps.say: This chest scan shows a nodular rind encasing the right lung with thickening along the mediastinal and fissural pleura and fluid in the pleural space. The picture fits malignant pleural mesothelioma linked to earlier asbestos contact. The rind explains persistent chest pain and shortness of breath. For exams, link unilateral effusion with nodular pleural thickening to mesothelioma and always ask about occupational exposure.

steps.tx: Definitive tissue diagnosis requires immunohistochemical confirmation to distinguish mesothelioma from pleural metastases of adenocarcinoma. Typical positive mesothelial markers are **calretinin**, WT1, cytokeratin 5/6, and podoplanin D2-40. Furthermore, diagnostic genomic testing reveals somatic BRCA1-associated protein 1 or **BAP1 loss** by immunohistochemistry in over fifty percent of cases, alongside homozygous deletion of CDKN2A on chromosome 9p21 detected via fluorescence in situ hybridization.

steps.tx: First-line dual immune checkpoint inhibition has transformed systemic therapy for unresectable malignant **pleural mesothelioma**. In the phase 3 **CheckMate 743** trial, combining **nivolumab** with **ipilimumab** yielded significant improvements in overall survival compared to standard platinum doublet chemotherapy containing **pemetrexed**. The clinical benefit proved especially pronounced in non-epithelioid histological subtypes, establishing dual checkpoint blockade as the preferred global standard of care for sarcomatoid and biphasic disease.

The clinical benefit proved especially pronounced in non-epithelioid histological subtypes.

steps.tx: For patients eligible for chemotherapy or displaying epithelioid histology, systemic doublet therapy combines **cisplatin** and **pemetrexed** with folic acid and vitamin B12 supplementation to reduce toxicity. In fit patients, adding the vascular endothelial growth factor inhibitor **bevacizumab** produces a further survival advantage according to the MAPS trial. Maintenance pemetrexed or subsequent rechallenge may be considered in carefully selected individuals retaining adequate renal and pulmonary functional reserve.

Treatment selection depends on patient performance status.

steps.tx: Thymic epithelial tumours originate in the anterior mediastinum and are staged pathologically by the modified **Masaoka-Koga** system. **Thymomas** range from stage 1 encapsulated lesions completely amenable to surgical excision, to invasive stage 4 tumours with pleural implants, pericardial dissemination, or lymphogenous metastases. The World Health Organization classifies thymomas histologically into types A, AB, B1, B2, and B3 based on the proportion of neoplastic epithelial cells versus non-neoplastic lymphocytes.
steps.say: Thymic epithelial tumours originate in the anterior mediastinum and are staged pathologically by the modified Masaoka-Koga system. Thymomas range from stage 1 encapsulated lesions completely amenable to surgical excision, to invasive stage 4 tumours with pleural implants or lymphogenous metastases. The WHO classifies thymomas histologically based on epithelial and lymphocytic components.

steps.tx: **Myasthenia gravis** is the most frequent autoimmune paraneoplastic disorder encountered in anterior mediastinal disease, occurring in approximately 30% to 40% of patients with thymoma. Circulating autoantibodies targeting nicotinic **acetylcholine receptor** complexes at the neuromuscular junction mediate fluctuating skeletal muscle weakness, ptosis, and diplopia. All patients diagnosed with an anterior mediastinal mass require baseline acetylcholine receptor antibody testing, and perioperative plasmapheresis may be indicated to prevent myasthenic crisis.

steps.tx: **Thymic carcinoma** represents an overtly malignant subtype characterized by severe **cytological atypia**, absence of immature T-lymphocytes, and high rates of capsular and vascular invasion. Immunohistochemical markers reveal strong positivity for CD5 and CD117 or KIT in thymic carcinoma, readily differentiating it from benign or low-grade thymomas. Because of aggressive biological behaviour, advanced presentations and early lymphatic or hematogenous metastases are commonplace at the time of initial clinical evaluation.

steps.tx: For unresectable or metastatic thymic carcinoma, platinum-based **systemic therapy** forms the backbone of palliative treatment. Regimens incorporating **carboplatin plus paclitaxel** or cisplatin, doxorubicin, and cyclophosphamide achieve meaningful objective tumour responses. In patients whose tumours possess specific KIT alterations, selective tyrosine kinase inhibitors provide clinical efficacy. Dual immunotherapy or pembrolizumab may provide salvage options, requiring vigilant monitoring for immune-mediated myocarditis.
